solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Very blue swan with a high voice

parts.note: a cob is a male swan
alto, shortened to alt, is a high singing voice; 'alt' also means high in pitch

explanation.surface: A swan that sings in a strikingly high register.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of a metal gives its name to a deep, intense shade of blue pigment.

clue.text: Sailor in unusual place is effective

indicators.note: in puts the sailor inside the rearranged letters
unusual says the letters come in an odd order

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman in an unfamiliar post still does well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sailor' is the usual crossword signal for AB, able seaman; the shuffled letters of 'place' are split around him.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone competent and able to get things done is effective.

clue.text: Once bit is broken, it makes two pieces

definitions.note: the definition describes the noun as the act that produces two parts

indicators.note: broken means smashed apart, so the letters are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: Once something is broken it lies in two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting something into two equal parts is the act of halving.

clue.text: A character in literature?

parts.note: a character here is a written symbol such as A or B, not a person in a novel

explanation.surface: A query about a figure in a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' suggests a fictional person, but it is a written symbol of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A single symbol of the alphabet is a written character.

clue.text: Oxford difficult to get into? Try this

definitions.text: Oxford difficult to get into? Try this

parts.words: Oxford difficult to get into? Try this
parts.note: an Oxford is a style of lace-up shoe, not the university; a tight shoe is eased on with a curved tool

explanation.surface: Advice to a hopeful applicant facing Oxford University's tough admissions.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like advice on university entrance, but an Oxford here is a laced leather shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved tool slipped into the heel helps a foot slide into tight footwear such as an Oxford.

clue.text: Horribly heartless, yet pure in heart

indicators.note: heartless says the central letters of the word are cut out

explanation.surface: A villain is cruel yet somehow innocent deep down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes RRIB from the middle of HORRIBLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Saintly and sinless people are spiritually pure.

clue.text: Inscriptions not the happiest — yet they could be

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters may be rearranged into a different word

explanation.surface: Gravestone words are rarely cheerful, though they might be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not the' is a link: these inscriptions are rarely happy, yet the letters of 'happiest' make them.
explanation.definitionFit: Words carved on a tombstone in memory of the dead are a kind of inscription.

clue.text: One has to be what one is

definitions.text: One has to be what one is

parts.words: One has to be what one is
parts.note: read as one has, in order to be this: a possessor is defined by having

explanation.surface: A philosophical shrug that people are what they are.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like resignation, but 'has' means possesses.
explanation.definitionFit: A proprietor is simply someone who possesses something.

clue.text: Unnecessary loss of a point irritates

indicators.note: loss of says the compass point is taken away

parts.note: needless means unnecessary
S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Dropping a point for no good reason annoys a player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loss of' takes an S off NEEDLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To provoke or annoy someone persistently with jibes is to goad them.

clue.text: Old foreign coin embedded in a vegetable

indicators.note: in places the word for embedded inside the vegetable

parts.note: a pea is a vegetable
set, as of a stone set firmly in place

explanation.surface: An old coin found stuck inside a vegetable, like a trinket in a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embedded' reads as the instruction to insert, but it is the word to be inserted: set, as in fixed firmly.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the currency of Spain before the euro replaced it in 2002.

clue.text: League match

definitions.meaning: a league is a union of parties or nations joined for a shared purpose
a match can be a marriage, a union of two families

explanation.definitionFit: Both a political union of states and a marriage are formal unions joining two or more parties.

clue.text: Nobleman takes the railway out of town

parts.note: a count is a European nobleman
RY is an abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: An aristocrat catches the train to leave the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural areas away from towns are described as the countryside, the rural districts.

clue.text: Composer has part played back for a single-minded man

parts.note: Johann Sebastian Bach, the German composer

indicators.note: played back, like a recording rewound, says the word for part is read backwards

parts.note: an actor's part is a role

explanation.surface: A musician hears a passage of his own work replayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played back' turns ROLE into ELOR. 'single-minded' is a pun: the man's mind is set on staying single.
explanation.definitionFit: An unmarried man is one who stays single, playfully called single-minded.

clue.text: Shrub that's evergreen — but not hardy we hear!

definitions.meaning: a bay is a glossy evergreen shrub of this family
of the comedy duo Stan and Oliver Hardy, this is the partner who is not Hardy, a name we hear often

explanation.surface: A gardener warns that an evergreen bush will not survive the frost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hardy' looks like gardening talk for frost-tolerant, but it is Oliver Hardy, the other half of the film comedy double act Laurel and Hardy.
explanation.definitionFit: Bay trees belong to the evergreen family whose leaves crowned victors; Stan of the comedy duo shares its name.

clue.text: Fifty-one line up endlessly on right for a drink

parts.note: LI is fifty-one in Roman numerals

indicators.note: endlessly says the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to queue is to line up

explanation.surface: Fifty-one people stand patiently in line at a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts QUEUE to QUEU.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet, flavoured spirit served after dinner is an alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Finish playing one's part

parts.note: an actor whose part in a scene is over leaves the stage, and the script marks this departure

explanation.surface: An actor completes their role.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage direction marks an actor's departure from the scene, and the word also means a way out.

clue.text: Is the Saint perplexed? Quite the opposite!

indicators.note: perplexed means muddled or tangled, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a holy man is puzzled and is told the reverse is true.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a direct contrast, the exact reverse of something.

clue.text: Hold forth about strike and be extravagant

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the words for hold forth go round the word for strike

parts.note: to spout is to hold forth, talk at length
to lash is to strike

explanation.surface: A speaker rants about industrial action and overspends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' suggests a walkout, but it means a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: To spend money freely and lavishly is a common phrasal verb meaning to indulge.

clue.text: Joined a non-drinker and suffered for it

parts.note: TT, teetotal, describes a non-drinker
ached means suffered pain

explanation.surface: Someone joined a teetotaller and paid for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fastened or connected to something means linked or fixed together.

clue.text: Maybe Rumania's about to become a health resort

indicators.note: about means around or astir, so the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A country's spa town is about to become a health destination.
explanation.walkthrough: Rumania is an older spelling of Romania; 'Maybe' and 'become' just link.
explanation.definitionFit: A clinic for convalescents or long-term patients, historically one in a healthy climate, is a place to recover.

clue.text: Model lass and her footwear?

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A fashion model shows off a girl's shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like a noun, but it is a verb meaning reshape.
explanation.definitionFit: Open shoes held on by straps are a kind of summer footwear.

clue.text: Part of the arm that is somewhat painful, naturally

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sore spot in the arm that naturally hurts a little.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft definition took in 'that', but 'Part of the arm' is the whole definition; 'that is' only links it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the two long bones of the forearm, on the little-finger side.

clue.text: Beasts of burden going round by deep gorges

indicators.note: going round means encircling, so the animals surround the small word

parts.note: asses, donkeys, are beasts of burden

explanation.surface: Pack animals pick their way around steep ravines.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottomless chasms or very deep pits are huge holes in the earth.

clue.text: Blurt out about article being vicious

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the article
out means wrong or off, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone says something cruel about a newspaper piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' shuffles BLURT to BRUTL; 'about' puts it round A.
explanation.definitionFit: Savagely cruel and violent behaviour is ferocious.

clue.text: Fair comment?

parts.note: fair comment is a legal defence in libel, but here it is a remark that something is fair or passable

explanation.surface: A query about whether a remark is a fair one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair comment' is a legal phrase, but read 'fair' as 'middling': the comment is what you say of something merely fair.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom of grudging approval, said of something reasonably good but not outstanding.

clue.text: It is up to a painter to provide jewellery

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is a painter

explanation.surface: It is the artist's job to supply the jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns IT into TI. RA is a Royal Academician, a member of London's Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewelled crescent-shaped headdress, like a small crown, is a piece of jewellery.

clue.text: Source of milk may provide us with energy

indicators.note: may provide suggests the letters can be worked into something new by rearranging them

explanation.surface: A dairy cow is praised for giving us energy.
explanation.walkthrough: The cow breed comes from the Channel Island of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of dairy cow from a Channel Island, prized for rich creamy milk.

clue.text: Military policeman is about to get mischief-makers

indicators.note: about means around, so the word is goes round the abbreviation

explanation.surface: A redcap is about to catch some troublemakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Small devils, or naughty children, are playful troublemakers.

clue.text: Article probing song on a curse

indicators.note: in an across answer, on means placed after
probing means poking into, so the article goes inside the word for song

parts.note: an anthem is a song of praise or loyalty
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A word in a hymn carries a curse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'probing' puts A inside ANTHEM to give ANATHEM.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a formal ban or curse, especially one pronounced by a church.

clue.text: Seats lost so need to be replaced

indicators.note: replaced here means put back in a different arrangement, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Chairs have gone missing and must be bought again.
explanation.definitionFit: Backless seats with legs are a kind of chair-like furniture.

clue.text: Negligent hit-and-run?

parts.note: a slap is a hit with the open hand
a dash is a quick run

explanation.surface: A careless driver who hits someone and flees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit-and-run' looks like the crime, but split it: a hit, then a run.
explanation.definitionFit: Hasty and careless work is described as done carelessly in a rush.

clue.text: Beastly slow Holst's composition?

definitions.note: the definition names creatures that are slow, a plural noun read as slow beasts

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so the letters are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A critic calls a piece by the composer Gustav Holst dreadfully plodding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beastly' looks like 'awful', but it means 'beasts': slow animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Tree-dwelling mammals of South America famous for their extremely slow movement.
